# Story 25.2: Enable flex-grow on header and body cells so columns spread to fill row width

Status: in-progress

## Story

As a developer,
I want `.dms-header-cell` and `.dms-body-cell` in `dms-base-table` to use `flex: 1 1 auto` so columns spread to fill the full row width while configured widths still render as their basis,
so that tables no longer leave unused space on wide viewports (the regression introduced by Story 10.3's `flex: 0 1 auto`) and configured column widths are preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The top-level `.dms-header-cell` rule in `base-table.component.scss` declares `flex: 1 1 auto;` (grow enabled, basis `auto`, shrink enabled).
2. The top-level `.dms-body-cell` rule in `base-table.component.scss` declares `flex: 1 1 auto;`.
3. Story 25.1's previously-skipped tests are unskipped and pass against the updated SCSS (both header and body rules match `/flex:\s*1\s+1\s+auto/`).
4. Configured column widths still render as each cell's flex-basis — a `ColumnDef.width` of 230px still starts at 230px before any grow distribution (Story 10.3 behavior preserved), and shrink stays enabled so narrow viewports can compress columns.
5. Header and body cells keep identical flex rules, so header/body column-width parity holds (the invariant asserted by `base-table-two-region-regression.spec.ts`).

- [ ] Task 1 (AC: #3): Confirm red against current SCSS.

  - [ ] 1.2 Run `nx test dms-material` and confirm BOTH tests FAIL against the current SCSS (`flex: 0 1 auto`) — red confirmed before implementing.

  - [ ] 2.1 In `base-table.component.scss`, change `.dms-header-cell`'s `flex: 0 1 auto;` to `flex: 1 1 auto;`.
  - [ ] 2.2 Change `.dms-body-cell`'s `flex: 0 1 auto;` to `flex: 1 1 auto;`. Keep the two rules identical so header/body parity holds.
- [ ] Task 3 (AC: #3, #4, #5): Confirm green and verify no regression.
  - [ ] 3.1 Run `nx test dms-material` and confirm both previously-red tests now pass.
  - [ ] 3.2 Verify the change is scoped to the two flex declarations only — no other SCSS or component-code edits in this story.

## Dev Notes

- **Why:** Story 10.3 introduced `flex: 0 1 auto` on both cell classes so the inline `[style.width.px]` binding (set from `column.width ?? DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH`) would take effect against Material MDC's default `mat-cell, mat-header-cell { flex: 1 }`. The grow=0 value fixed "configured widths ignored" but disabled expansion, so cells now occupy exactly their configured width and the row no longer fills — columns stopped spreading over the full table width. Restoring grow (`flex: 1 1 auto`) keeps basis = configured width (so Story 10.3's fix still holds) while letting spare row width distribute across columns.
- **Mechanism:** with `flex-basis: auto`, each cell's inline `[style.width.px]` becomes its starting size; `flex-grow: 1` then distributes any remaining row width proportionally, and `flex-shrink: 1` preserves the existing narrow-viewport compression behavior. Header and body cells must stay identical so header/body parity (asserted in e2e) is preserved.
- **Do NOT** change the inline `[style.width.px]` binding in `base-table.component.html`, the `DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH` constant, or any other SCSS rule — only the two flex declarations.
- The Epic request suspected Epic 20 caused this; Epic 20 was theming-only (`--dms-*` tokens into Tailwind `theme.extend` + dead-class removal) and never touched table layout. Story 10.3 is the actual regression source (see Dev Notes in epics.md).
